title: Regal Theater band under Dave Payton, 1929-30
summary: Levy turns from violin to banjo and joins the Regal Theater band, getting the job from Bud Scott. They play shows and band numbers, with Fess Williams then Harold Bacquet fronting.

bands.name: Fess Williams and His Joy Boys

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You started as an arranger, didn't you? No, I started, I started playing violin. I was with this man playing violin. Well, I mean with your writing though, you started with the banjo. Uh-huh.

And, uh, the banjo became so prominent, prominent that I got a banjo. And, uh, then I went to the Regal Theater in 1929 and we had a wonderful band there. We had Red Top playing trumpet and he was later with Cab Callaway, he was playing a tremendous trumpet.

Dave Payton, yeah. And we played all the toughest shows and played band numbers too. Every week we had to play a band number. And they featured me several times on the banjo. I played the world's waiting for sunrise, you know, Melvin' Chords and whipped it up. And several other numbers. Hebe-jeebies I think was another one we used to play there.
Wasn't Bud Scott also there? Did you play by?

Bud Scott gave me the job. Oh. Bud Scott, his wife went to California and she liked it so well that, uh, she told him, come on out here, I'm not coming back. So Bud met me on the speech and said, Charlie, I want you to have that job. And, uh, and he said, I told Dave Payton, he said that you can come up and cut everything they got on the paper and then a little more too. I said, oh, I think I can do that. I said, alright.
You have to do that to work with Dave. Yeah.

Oh yeah. Yes, yeah. Yes. Yes. And, uh, so Bud Scott told me, he said, you come around and see Dave, come on. He says, I got to go to California. My wife won't come back to me, say, come out there, she's crazy about California.
Was that before or after Fess Williams?
No, Fess Williams was, uh, no, Fess Williams was there. Then Fess Williams left and Harold Bacquet came and he was a master of ceremonies.
But you were there a while during Fess?
I was there, 29 and 30, yeah, 1929 and 30.

Did you happen to record with Fess Williams? I was there, they made, uh, one record in the name of Fess and his Joy Boys or something. But that might have been earlier. No, I think that was some of the, that was a little earlier.
